::: {#rem-confidence-interval-exact}
#### Exact intervals and confidence sets

The probability in @def-confidence-interval
is the [coverage probability](#def-coverage-probability) of $\cintf{X}$,
which can depend on $\param$.
The infimum of the coverage probability over $\param$
is the interval's **confidence coefficient**,
and the definition requires it to be at least $1 - \siglevel$.
An interval is **exact** when the coverage probability equals $1 - \siglevel$
for every $\param$;
discrete data usually allow only a conservative interval,
whose coverage probability is larger than $1 - \siglevel$
for some $\param$.
A region that need not be an interval is a **confidence set**
[@CaseBerg01, Section 9.1].
:::
